messages.author: Maria Chen (CyberSynth)
messages.content:
## [**Maria Chen**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/fakeprofile1) 

*Founder & Lead AI Architect @ [CyberSynth](https://cybersynth.dev) · We build secure, decentralized AI systems.*

Hi everyone! I've been in the cybersecurity space for over a decade, transitioning into AI security about 3 years ago. I'm a big believer in open-source and building tools that empower developers. In my other life, I'm a competitive rock climber.

Special power: Can debug race conditions in my sleep.

📍 San Francisco, CA (PST)

messages.author: David Lee (DataWeave)
messages.content:
## [**David Lee**](https://www.linkedin.com/in/fakeprofile2)
*Head of Data @ [DataWeave](https://dataweave.io) · Making data pipelines intelligent and autonomous.*

Hello! I'm David. I've been wrestling with large-scale data systems for my entire career, from Hadoop clusters to modern data lakes. Now I'm focused on applying LLMs to data engineering workflows. I also contribute to Apache Arrow.

Special power: I roast my own coffee beans. The perfect pour-over is my art form.

📍 London, UK (GMT)

messages.author: Sofia Rodriguez (LogicLoom)
messages.content:
## [Sofia Rodriguez](https://www.linkedin.com/in/fakeprofile3)

*Co-founder & CEO @ [LogicLoom](https://logicoom.ai) · LogicLoom is a platform for building and verifying complex agentic workflows. Think of it as unit testing for AI agents.*

Hey all! I'm a former philosophy professor turned tech entrepreneur. My passion is at the intersection of formal logic and machine learning. LogicLoom is my attempt to bring more rigor and reliability to the AI space.

Special power: I can recite the first 200 digits of pi. It's a completely useless but fun party trick.

📍 Berlin, DE (CET)

messages.author: Fatima Al-Jamil (Synthax)
messages.content: Really insightful talk on data synthesis.

messages.author: Fatima Al-Jamil (Synthax)
messages.content: For anyone interested in the future of synthetic data for training, this talk from the 'AI Engineering' summit was fantastic.

embeds.title: Synthetic Data: The Key to Unlocking AGI? - AI Engineering Summit 2024
embeds.description: Dr. Eva Rostova explores cutting-edge techniques for generating high-quality synthetic data and its impact on model performance and safety.

messages.author: Chloe Dubois (Aether AI)
messages.content: We just open-sourced our model quantization toolkit! Would love to get feedback from the community.

embeds.title: Announcing AetherLite: Our Open-Source Quantization Library
embeds.description: Developers can now use AetherLite to shrink and accelerate their models for deployment on edge devices with minimal performance loss.

messages.author: Kenji Tanaka (NeuroNet)
messages.content: Our work on generative graph networks was featured by Google AI's research blog!

embeds.title: NeuroNet's Groundbreaking Research in Graph-based RAG
embeds.description: Highlighting a new approach that combines Knowledge Graphs with LLMs for more accurate and explainable responses. A collaborative effort with leading academics...

messages.author: Ethan Brown (CodeFlow)
messages.content: We've finally released v1.0 of the Plakar backup format! A modern, content-addressable format for data snapshots. No more tarballs!

embeds.title: Plakar v1.0: A New Era for Data Backups
embeds.description: Moving beyond legacy formats, Plakar offers speed, deduplication, and encryption for modern data protection needs.

messages.author: Alex Ivanov (CogniCore)
messages.content: A new contender for the best locally-runnable model is here. Chimera-7B from Phoenix Labs. 64B total params, ~7B active. Smaller than Llama3 8B, faster than Mistral Medium. The architecture is wild.

embeds.title: phoenix-labs/Chimera-7B-Instruct · Hugging Face
embeds.description: Model card for Chimera-7B-Instruct, a new sparse mixture-of-experts model.

messages.author: Alex Ivanov (CogniCore)
messages.content: Just got the new Chimera-7B model running with the latest optimizations. Hitting 90 tokens/sec on a single 4090. This is wild for a Mixture-of-Experts model.

messages.author: Fatima Al-Jamil (Synthax)
messages.content: Also, the new Finch series of models from Baidu looks very strong. They have a version with a persistent memory architecture which is fascinating.

embeds.title: Introducing the Finch Model Family
embeds.description: We are open-sourcing our new family of language models, Finch, featuring dense and MoE variants, and a novel long-context memory mechanism.

messages.author: Ava Singh (Quantum Works)
messages.content: I just published a new post on the missing architectural layers in the Generative AI stack. With MCP gaining traction, it highlights the need for more standardized protocols to build robust and scalable AI systems. Would love to hear your thoughts!

embeds.title: The Generative AI Infrastructure Gap: 8 Protocols We Need Now
embeds.description: The rapid evolution of AI is creating architectural debt. These are the 8 critical patterns and protocols we need to define to build the next generation of AI infrastructure.

messages.author: Noah Kim (Apex Dynamics)
messages.content: Big news: MCP now supports authentication via common providers. This is a huge step forward for security.

embeds.title: Securing Your Agents: MCP Now Supports Authentication
embeds.description: You can now protect your MCP servers and require user authentication before an AI agent can access its tools. Here's a quick demo showing how to implement it...

messages.author: Kenji Tanaka (NeuroNet)
messages.content: I will never, ever let an agent connect directly to a production database via MCP. That's a recipe for disaster.
